5:- A topic's description and outcome together may ask about more than one thing. Judge the one the topic's outcome names as what is tracked. List every other part of the topic's description and outcome that the question leaves out, a second figure or event, a condition or a comparison, in not_judged, each with one sentence on why it is not the one tracked. A second side of the same bet, for example a market's tightness beside the volume shipped, a share beside the total it is part of, or capacity beside the demand it serves, stays in the one question as context: list it in not_judged. A second side is not by itself a reason to decline; decline only when no part is the main one, or when the main part itself meets a case below. Never fold two things into one ladder: "Will the regulator approve the drug for a second use, and how many patients will take it in the first year?" is judged on the approval when that is what its outcome names, and the patient count is listed; "How much will the carrier's fuel bill be next year, and will its pilots strike?" is judged on the fuel bill when that is what its outcome names, and the strike is listed.
6:- Return no_ladder with the reason, and ladder null, in seven cases: the topic has no main figure or event, naming none, or naming several with none of them the main one; nothing in the topic can be checked on a date, which for an event means that neither the topic nor the item gives a date and the topic names no period, unless it is a pending regulatory decision, for which use the company's current fiscal year-end; the figure is a company's figure for a quarter or a half-year, which is evidence to a yearly question; the figure covers a period that is not one fiscal or calendar year, such as a survey's rolling twelve months, and neither the topic nor the item gives the day it is published; the figure is for a year that has already ended on the item's day; the figure is for a year beyond next year, unless the topic's opens_as is binding_obligation; or the question belongs to another company or to a matter that no theme in the request's themes covers, in which case name that company or matter in the reason. Do not rewrite a figure for a year beyond next year as an event to keep it; a numeric completion target may define the state of an event that is itself the topic.
9:- A question about the company's revenue, profit, share, product progress or its own obligations is about the company: object is its ticker, even when policy or macroeconomics drives it. A question about what happens in the world, such as licensing, interest rates or aggregate spending, rather than the resulting effect on one company, belongs to a theme: object is a theme id from the request's themes. A question whose tracked outcome is a government's or regulator's decision to permit, restrict or ban a class of products or trade belongs to the theme that covers it, also when the product is the company's own: whether a health ministry lifts its import ban on one drug maker's vaccine belongs to the theme that covers that country's drug approvals. When the tracked outcome is the company's own sales, shipments or revenue under such a decision, the question is about the company, as is a proceeding against the company itself, such as an investigation of its conduct or a fine. A question about another company's own figure, or about a matter no listed theme covers, has no object here: return no_ladder.

**The three round-75 fixes are present, but I found one remaining mismatch in the recovery rule.** I would not send until it is settled.

The reading form has a **G** mark for whether a figure’s ranges are a fair division around the amount in the article. The scorer’s `failed_marks()` iterates over `accounting.marks_that_apply()`, which deliberately excludes G, and `correct_written()` sees only that resulting set. Consequently, a figure answer with **G = fails** and no other failed mark can count as a “correct recovery,” contrary to the design’s “no mark settled as failing.” [Reading form]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/stage-a-reader-brief.md:102), [accounting]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_a/accounting.py:36), [scorer]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/probe_score.py:92)

Decide before the send whether G belongs in the recovery criterion. If it does, define how its `not_assessable` and disputed values are treated and test a G-failing recovery. If it remains a separate diagnostic, say explicitly that “correct” means **no failed gate-accounted mark**, report G beside each recovery, and avoid claiming the answer choices are wholly sound.

The requested fixes otherwise check out: a code refusal cannot retain a refusal control, failed L/W/H marks prevent a recovery from counting, and N and code refusals remain in the harm comparison. The saved tests and mutant log address those distinctions. The two-arm comparison and conditional spending limit are also stated. [Design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/DESIGN-A2.md:47), [mutant log]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/test-mutants.txt)

CONSENSUS: no, because G is a reader mark the stated “correct recovery” rule does not account for or explicitly exclude.
